title: Kohli Is Out. He Played Through the Hamstring Strain in the Final. Now He Will Miss the Entire Afghanistan ODI Series.
excerpt: Ruturaj Gaikwad replaces Kohli in the ODI squad. Rajat Patidar is in line for India A. The BCCI has advised at least two weeks of rest.
body:
Virat Kohli has been ruled out of the three-match ODI series against Afghanistan after sustaining a hamstring injury during the IPL 2026 final. Chennai Super Kings captain Ruturaj Gaikwad is set to replace him, while RCB skipper Rajat Patidar may be drafted into the India A squad for the Sri Lanka tri-series.

The injury struck during the most dramatic possible moment. In the final at Ahmedabad on May 31, Kohli felt a strain in his right hamstring while batting during RCB's successful chase against Gujarat Titans. The physio was summoned to the field. Kohli had the injured area heavily strapped, but he refused to leave. He stayed at the crease and hit the winning runs, finishing the tournament with 675 runs at an average of 56.25 and a career-high strike rate above 165.

Medical tests after the match confirmed a hamstring strain. The BCCI has advised at least two weeks of rest. Though Kohli could theoretically be fit by the third ODI on June 20, the Ajit Agarkar-led selection committee has decided against bringing him back mid-series. "He is out of the ODI series due to a hamstring injury," a BCCI source confirmed to PTI.

## Gaikwad Steps In

Ruturaj Gaikwad's selection as the replacement is a reward for consistency. The 28-year-old CSK captain scored a century on his ODI return against South Africa in December 2025, after nearly two years away from the squad. He had originally been named in the India A squad for the tri-series in Sri Lanka as a replacement for the injured Riyan Parag. Now he steps up to the senior side.

If Gaikwad is elevated, Rajat Patidar — who led RCB to back-to-back IPL titles — becomes the frontrunner to take his India A spot. Patidar last played an ODI for India in 2023 against South Africa. His sensational IPL 2026 captaincy campaign, which saw RCB lift consecutive trophies, has put him firmly back in the conversation for international selection.

## The Rohit Question

Rohit Sharma's availability for the ODIs also remains conditional. The Indian captain sustained a hamstring issue during his appearances for Mumbai Indians in IPL 2026. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar has said that Rohit's participation is "subject to fitness clearance" at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence. If Rohit is also ruled out, Yashasvi Jaiswal is likely to be called up as an additional replacement.

## The Bigger Picture

The timing of Kohli's setback carries implications beyond this series. India are scheduled to tour England in July for three ODIs and three T20Is, and the 2027 Champions Trophy cycle looms. At 37, every injury layoff raises louder questions about how many more white-ball tours Kohli will commit to.

For now, the Afghanistan series — three ODIs in Dharamsala (June 13), Lucknow (June 17), and Chennai (June 20), preceded by a one-off Test at Mohali starting June 6 — will proceed without the man who defined Indian batting for a generation. The squad, captained by Shubman Gill, includes Shreyas Iyer as vice-captain, with KL Rahul and Ishan Kishan as wicketkeeping options.

For the millions of NRI fans who stayed up past midnight to watch Kohli bat in the IPL final, the news is a reminder that the body has its limits, even when the will does not.
